title: He warns you now so you never have to face it.
subtitle: A warning given out of care
then: After naming the loss of self and family, the verse describes the Fire in one line. Ibn Kathir says Allah tells us this {idea}so that His servants keep away from sin.{/idea} It ends tenderly: O My servants.
now: A parent grabs a child's hand at the edge of a busy road and shouts. It sounds harsh, but it is love. {idea}The warning comes first so the harm never does.{/idea} And notice He still calls you His.
old: Verses about the Fire are only meant to scare me.
new: He warns because He wants me safe, and He still calls me His servant.
try: Think of one habit you know is harmful, and take one step away from it today.

title: Good news for those who walked away from false gods.
subtitle: Turning away and turning back
then: Ibn Kathir reports it was said to be about Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr and Salman al-Farisi, men who {idea}left idol worship and searched for the truth.{/idea} The correct view, he says, is that it covers everyone like them.
now: You quit the thing that was ruling your evenings: the game, the feed, the late nights. But an empty hour fills up again fast. {idea}Leaving is half. Turning to Him is the other half.{/idea}
old: Giving up a bad thing is enough.
new: The good news is for those who leave false masters and also turn back to Allah.
try: Take one hour you used to spend on a habit you dropped, and give ten minutes of it to Allah.

title: Listen to everything, follow the best of it.
subtitle: How guided people listen
then: Ibn Kathir says these are the ones who {idea}understand the Word and act on it{/idea}, like Musa told to take the Tawrah firmly and have his people take the best in it.
now: You finish a talk on your commute and think: that was good. By lunch you cannot remember one point. {idea}Pick the best line and live it today.{/idea}
old: Hearing a good reminder is the same as benefiting from it.
new: Guidance is listening closely and then following the best of what I heard.
try: From the next reminder you hear, pick one line and act on it before the day ends.

title: You cannot save someone; only Allah guides.
subtitle: The limit of what you can do for others
then: The question is put to the Prophet ﷺ himself: can you rescue one who is in the Fire? Ibn Kathir explains {idea}no one can guide him apart from Allah.{/idea} The Prophet's ﷺ task was to convey.
now: Your brother has stopped praying. You have tried every argument, sent every video. You lie awake feeling it is your failure. {idea}Keep caring, keep praying for him, and put the weight down.{/idea}
old: If someone I love goes astray, I have failed.
new: My job is to care and convey; guiding hearts belongs to Allah alone.
try: Make dua tonight, by name, for one person you have been trying to change.

title: Rooms built above rooms, with rivers below.
subtitle: A promise Allah does not break
then: Ibn Kathir reports the Prophet ﷺ said there are rooms in Paradise seen from inside and out, and when asked who they are for, said: {reward}those who speak kindly, feed others, and pray at night while people sleep.{/reward}
now: You save for years for a small flat, checking listings every night. The verse points to a home that no inflation touches. {reward}And the price is kind words, a shared meal, and a quiet prayer.{/reward}
old: Paradise feels too far away to think about.
new: It is a promise Allah never breaks, built by ordinary kindness and night prayer.
try: Feed someone today: a neighbor, a coworker, or a stranger, even with something small.

title: Green, then yellow, then dust. So is this life.
subtitle: The life of a crop as a mirror
then: Ibn Kathir says this is a reminder that {idea}this world is green and fresh, then it grows old.{/idea} The young man becomes old and weak, then death comes. The blessed one is whose state after death is good.
now: You scroll back through photos from ten years ago. The face, the energy, the friends who were always around. {idea}The field always turns yellow.{/idea} The question is what you planted while it was green.
old: I have plenty of time; I am still young.
new: Every green season turns, so I should invest in what lasts beyond it.
try: Look at an old photo of yourself today and ask: what good did I do since then?

title: An open chest with light, or a heart gone hard.
subtitle: Two hearts hearing the same remembrance

key.label: The sign of a hard heart

then: Right after the image of a field drying out, the verse turns to hearts. Ibn Kathir says the hard-hearted {trap}do not become soft when Allah is mentioned.{/trap} The open heart {reward}is on light from its Lord.{/reward}
now: The imam recites a verse that once made you cry. Now you are checking the time. Nothing moves. {idea}A heart can dry out like a field, and it can be watered again.{/idea}
old: Feeling nothing in prayer is just how it is now.
new: A heart that stops softening is a warning sign, and Allah can open it again.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to soften your heart.

title: Skin shivers, then the heart settles.
subtitle: How the best speech moves those who fear Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Quran pairs things: believers then disbelievers, Paradise then Hell. So {trap}the warnings make skin shiver{/trap}, then {reward}hope softens the heart.{/reward} Qatadah said they wept quietly; they did not lose their minds.
now: Late at night you play a recitation with headphones. One verse makes the hair on your arm rise. A few verses later you feel calm. {idea}Fear, then hope. That is the Book working.{/idea}
old: Being moved by the Quran means big emotion.
new: The real sign is a quiet shiver of fear and then a heart at rest.
try: Listen to one page of Quran with a translation tonight, slowly, and notice where you feel it.

title: Nothing left to shield him but his own face.
subtitle: Not equal to the one who comes safe
then: After the soft hearts of the last verse comes the other side. Ibn Kathir says the wrongdoer is rebuked: {trap}taste what you used to earn.{/trap} Is he like the one who comes secure on the Day? The answer is left to you.
now: Every small cruelty, every lie that saved you trouble, every unkind word goes into a ledger you never see. {idea}What comes back is what you sent ahead.{/idea} And you can still change what you send.
old: What happens to me after death is out of my hands.
new: What I meet on the Day is what I earned, so I can start earning safety now.
try: Undo one small wrong today: an apology, a returned item, a corrected word.

title: It came from where they never looked.
subtitle: The danger of feeling safe
then: Ibn Kathir says earlier generations who denied their Messengers {trap}were destroyed for their sins, and none could protect them.{/trap} The Quraysh were being reminded that the same could reach them.
now: You keep saying you will fix it later: the prayer, the debt, the relative you stopped talking to. You assume you will get a warning first. {idea}Later is not promised to arrive with notice.{/idea}
old: I will sort things out when I see the end coming.
new: It often comes from where no one looks, so the time to set things right is now.
try: Pick one thing you keep postponing with Allah or a person, and do the first step today.

title: Disgrace here was small next to what comes after.
subtitle: If they only knew
then: Ibn Kathir says the earlier deniers tasted disgrace in this life, and {trap}what is promised in the Hereafter is worse.{/trap} So those addressed, who rejected the Seal of the Prophets ﷺ, should beware.
now: You are terrified of being embarrassed: caught out at work, exposed in the group chat. You will do almost anything to avoid that shame. {idea}Fear the account that lasts more than the one that fades.{/idea}
old: Public shame is the worst thing that could happen to me.
new: Worldly disgrace passes; what I face before Allah is what really matters.
try: Tonight, ask yourself which you worry about more: people's opinion or Allah's. Be honest.

title: Every kind of example, so you will remember.
subtitle: Why the Quran teaches in pictures
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah explains things {idea}by setting forth examples and parables, because they bring the meaning closer to people's minds.{/idea} Some are drawn from people's own lives.
now: You forget the lecture but remember the teacher's story about the broken vase. Pictures stick. {idea}The Quran's examples are made to stick.{/idea} When you meet one, ask where you are in it.
old: The parables in the Quran are about other people.
new: Each example is set out so I can see myself and remember.
try: Next time you read a parable in the Quran, write one line on where you see yourself in it.

title: Plain words with no crookedness in them.
subtitle: A clear Book, so you can be mindful

row.title: taqwa
sub: heed the warning, seek the promise

then: Ibn Kathir explains it is {idea}in a plain Arabic tongue, with no crookedness, deviation or confusion.{/idea} It was revealed this way so people would heed its warnings and strive for its promises.
now: You keep the Quran on a high shelf, thinking it is too deep for you. Then you read a single page with a translation and find it speaking directly. {idea}It was built to be understood.{/idea}
old: The Quran is too complex for someone like me.
new: It was sent plain and straight so that I could understand it and be mindful.
try: Read one short surah with its translation today, start to finish.

title: Many quarreling masters, or one Master.
subtitle: The exhausted servant and the settled one
then: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said this is {idea}the parable of the idolater and the sincere believer.{/idea} One slave is fought over by partners; the other belongs to one man. Ibn Kathir says the answer is so clear the verse ends with praise.
now: Your boss wants one thing, your in-laws another, your followers a third, your own ego a fourth. You are worn out trying to please them all. {trap}Many masters.{/trap} {reward}Serve One, and the rest fall into place.{/reward}
old: I have to keep everyone happy.
new: Belonging to Allah alone frees me from being torn between many masters.
try: Next decision you face today, ask only: what would please Allah here?
